pr_body:
Motivation:

[DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8484) wraps DNS queries inside HTTP request and sends it over TLS to make sure queries are secure in transit.

Modification:

Add DoHQueryEncoder and DoHResponseDecoder.
Add DoHClient Example

Result:
DoHClient Example
DoHQueryEncoder and DoHResponseDecoder for DNS queries encoding and decoding.

Fixes #9091.

The quirks that hit me were:

Submitting two requests since you can't query A and AAAA in same message.

Bootstrapping the resolver IP. Since it's questionable to rely on a DNS query to activate your DoH impl.
And restricting this to only public domain names. Since private IP addresses won't resolve via public hosted providers. Intranets will handle those internally.

@normanmaurer Is it fine to use builder instead of constructors? Because there are lots of configuration that can be applied and doing this with constructors will create more complications. What are your thoughts on this?

issue_context.title: DNS over HTTPS (DoH) and DNS Over TLS (DoT) Support
issue_context.body:
Any Plans To Support DNS over HTTPS (DoH) or DNS over TLS (DoT) in Netty?

DoH: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8484
DoT: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7858
comments: No no plans at all atm. That said we are happy to review contributions

review_comments: this depends on the fact that would have the adapter in the pipeline. I wonder if we should just not support http2 for now
or maybe we should better use `Http2Frame`s
The thing is, HTTP/2 is RECOMMENDED by RFC for DoH. I am looking for a better approach to handle this.
+1 to HTTP/2, I think you need 2 http requests to serve a normal DNS lookup.  And there is hopefully a high chance of reuse depending on number of distinct host lookups and the TTL.
assert return value
assert return value
you need to call `defaultDnsResponse.release()`
as this class is abstract we should use `protected` here
`tryFailure`
`<DnsQuery>`
final

Are you taking into account the cache rules at this point? https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8484#section-5.1

For example the TTL for records with non zero age?

We're not using any cache here. For now, this pull request is a basic implementation of DoH transport with no cache or what-so-ever. I have plans for Cache, QueryDecoder, and ResponseEncoder in the future.
I mainly meant that you are dropping the cache headers which can affect the implied TTL in the records.
Now I get it. Give me some time, I am on it now.
@hyperxpro let me know once resolved

@yschimke I read RFC completely. HTTP Header for Caching is useful when we've some sort of caching layer in Netty. For now, we don't have. With that said, users can definitely add their caching own solution at the DnsQuery handler.
use `embeddedChannel.finish()` and assert the return value

For now, only supporting `FullHttpResponse` because DNS responses are 1 shot. So If `HttpObject` is not an instance `FullHttpResponse` then we'll throw an error,
you need to call `fullHttpRequest.release()`
